name: Chin filler

card.summary: Injectable filler (usually hyaluronic acid) placed at the chin to add projection or length without surgery; temporary, with rare but serious vascular complications.
card.aka: Chin augmentation with filler, liquid genioplasty
card.note: Rare vascular occlusion and tissue necrosis are documented; self-injection by forum users is outside any regulated setting.

quick.overview:
Chin filler is a non-surgical way to add volume to the chin, most often with hyaluronic acid gel injected by a clinician. Companies have run registered trials of several products specifically for chin retrusion, and published case reviews describe its use for reshaping the facial profile.

On looksmax.org it is discussed as a trial run before surgery or a temporary alternative to implants and genioplasty. Forum members also post self-injection accounts, which clinicians regard as outside normal safety conditions.
quick.mechanism: Hyaluronic acid or similar gel is injected near the bone to add volume, projecting or lengthening the chin. The effect lasts as long as the material persists in the tissue and is reversible with hyaluronidase for hyaluronic acid products.
quick.risks: The chin is generally regarded as a lower-risk injection area, but case reports describe vascular occlusion, skin necrosis and even tongue necrosis after chin filler. Anatomical studies map the arteries to inform safer injection. Fillers are regulated medical devices administered by licensed practitioners.

lead: Chin filler is a non-surgical cosmetic treatment in which an injectable gel, most often hyaluronic acid, is placed in and around the chin to increase its projection, height or contour. It is sometimes called a liquid genioplasty. For appearance, adding volume at the point of the chin can make a receding chin look more forward, lengthen a short one, and make the jaw and neck line read more defined, with results that are immediate and, for hyaluronic acid, temporary.[1][3][10][20]

The US FDA approved two hyaluronic acid fillers for mild to moderate chin retrusion in adults, Juvederm Voluma XC in June 2020 and Restylane Defyne in February 2021, according to trade-press reports.[19][20] Manufacturers have registered further trials of chin products, and published literature includes a case review of 83 patients treated with combined forehead, nose and chin filler to alter the profile.[1][4][5][6]

The literature also documents rare serious complications, including vascular occlusion with skin and tongue necrosis, which is managed with the enzyme hyaluronidase when the filler is hyaluronic acid.[2][7][21] In looksmaxxing communities chin filler is discussed as a reversible, lower-cost alternative or precursor to chin implants and sliding genioplasty; forum members also post accounts of self-injection, which clinicians regard as outside normal safety conditions.[8][9][16][20]

chain: Gel is placed at or near the chin bone
Soft-tissue chin moves forward or lengthens
Stronger profile and clearer jaw-to-neck line
angle.text: Filler adds volume at the chin so a receding or short chin looks more projected, immediately and without surgery. People use it to improve profile balance, to preview what an implant or genioplasty might look like, or as a temporary alternative that lasts about as long as the product persists.

paras: The filler is deposited in or near the chin's soft tissue and over the bone to move the soft-tissue pogonion forward or lengthen the chin. Injectable fillers in general are substances made to be injected into connective tissue; hyaluronic acid is the most common because it occurs naturally in vertebrates, and most such gels are cross-linked to last longer.[17] Hyaluronic acid forms a gel with water, is injected with a needle or a blunt micro-cannula, and its effect is reported to last about 6 to 12 months in facial use.[18]

An encyclopedic summary of chin surgery lists hyaluronic acid and calcium hydroxyapatite as temporary fillers and notes that permanent silicone fillers have fallen out of favour because of migration, chronic inflammation and infection risks.[10] Dermatology Times quotes surgeon Michael Somenek as describing hyaluronic acid chin filler as lasting about 9 to 12 months, while PMMA filler such as Bellafill lasts longer and has a semi-permanent effect; he also reports being a trainer and speaker for Galderma and a speaker for Suneva.[20]
A published technique paper describes a multilayered cannula approach to the chin, and a case series proposes a profile algorithm combining forehead, nose, lip and chin filler.[1][11]

Hyaluronic acid was first isolated in 1934 by Karl Meyer and John Palmer from the vitreous body of cattle eyes, and Pharmacia developed the first hyaluronan biomedical product, Healon, for eye surgery in the 1970s and 1980s.[18] Dermal fillers became widely used through the 1980s, and in the US the FDA regulates them as medical devices.[17]

Trade reports date the first FDA chin-specific approvals to Juvederm Voluma XC in June 2020 and Restylane Defyne in February 2021, the latter for mild to moderate chin retrusion in adults.[19][20] Defyne had been first approved in 2016 for moderate to severe deep facial wrinkles and folds.[19] Registered trials since then have studied further products, including Restylane Lyft with lidocaine, Restylane Shaype against Juvederm Volux, and Stylage XXL in Chinese adults.[4][6][13][14]
Chin surgery has a longer history: Wikipedia cites a 1958 report by Aufricht on combined nose and chin surgery, and later comparisons of bone-based and synthetic chin augmentation.[10]

Hyaluronic acid gels differ in cross-linking, stiffness and lifting capacity; firmer gels are used where projection is wanted over bone. Calcium hydroxyapatite and PMMA-based products are also used in the lower face by some practitioners, with longer persistence than hyaluronic acid.[10][20] Polylactic acid fillers work by stimulating collagen rather than adding immediate volume.[17]

Practitioners describe technique variations including cannula versus needle placement, layering at different depths, and treating the chin together with the jawline or lips as a profile plan.[1][11] One Phase 4 registration evaluates filler for chin profile enhancement, chin asymmetry and jawline contour deficit, and another evaluates a jaw-contouring filler.[15][24]

Company-reported results for Restylane Defyne's pivotal trial, as relayed by a trade publication, state that 74 percent of patients had improved chin projection on the manufacturer's chin retrusion scale, that 99 percent reported improved chin appearance at 12 weeks and that improvement was reported for up to a year.[19] These figures originate with the manufacturer's announcement.

Surgical summaries note that bone-based changes usually produce a more dramatic correction than implants or filler, and that filler suits patients who prefer immediate, adjustable, reversible changes.[10][20] Somenek states that nearly all patients can receive filler, that results are immediate with little to no downtime, and that he favours filler over custom implants for asymmetry because it allows more precise contouring.[20]

Wikipedia lists bruising, redness, pain and itching as common filler effects, and infection, allergic reaction, scarring and lumps as less common ones.[17] In the Restylane Defyne trial summary, 86 percent of patients had no treatment-related adverse events, 23 of 24 reported events were mild, and the one moderate event was injection-site pain.[19]

The most serious filler complication is vascular occlusion, in which filler enters or compresses an artery. A 2018 emergency-medicine case report calls it rare but potentially detrimental and describes retrograde flow to the retinal arteries as a mechanism of vision loss in other facial areas.[22] Wikipedia notes that blindness from embolization into the ophthalmic and retinal arteries is usually permanent when it occurs and that delayed skin necrosis can follow embolization.[17]

A study using three-dimensional tomography and cadaveric dissection of 40 heads examined chin anatomy to discuss the avoidance of intravascular embolization.[3] A case series reported unilateral tongue necrosis from vascular occlusion after hyaluronic acid chin augmentation, stating that chin filler is considered a safe injection area and that this complication is rare.[2] A 2026 case report describes vascular occlusion after a low-volume chin injection managed with pulsed hyaluronidase.[7]

The Complications in Medical Aesthetics Collaborative's 2021 guideline calls hyaluronidase the mainstay of treatment for cross-linked hyaluronic acid occlusion, highly effective at preventing necrosis when given rapidly, and advises stopping injection immediately when occlusion is suspected, noting that a negative aspiration test does not rule occlusion out.[21]

Chin implants (silicone, porous polyethylene, ePTFE) and sliding genioplasty carry their own risks, including swelling, hematoma, lip numbness, infection, implant displacement and nerve injury.[10] Somenek describes implant results as generally permanent, with malposition and infection as the main concerns, and filler's main concern as intravascular injection near vessels and nerves.[20] A registered trial compares fat or PEEK onlay augmentation with sliding genioplasty for deficient chin.[25]

In the US, the FDA regulates dermal fillers as medical devices, and a licensed provider performs the injection; six fillers were reported approved there against over 140 on the UK and European market, where a CE mark does not require proof of medical efficacy.[17] Hyaluronic acid can be degraded by hyaluronidase enzymes, which clinicians use to reverse hyaluronic acid filler.[18][21] Self-administration outside a clinical setting is not part of any published evaluation, and the wiki does not reproduce procedural instructions.

Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article describes a spectrum from softmaxxing, such as skincare, grooming and fitness, to hardmaxxing, which includes cosmetic surgery such as jaw surgery.[23] Chin filler sits in between in community discussion: it is cosmetic and procedural but reversible, so members describe it as a way to test chin changes before surgery.[8][9]

Forum members ask whether chin filler would improve their profile, post transformation photographs, and discuss it alongside jaw and cheek filler.[8][9][12] Some threads document members injecting themselves or friends.[16] Published literature on complications concerns professional administration and anatomy.[2][3]

A case review of 83 consecutive patients treated with forehead, nose and chin filler assessed profile measurements and complications.[1] A manufacturer's pivotal trial of Restylane Defyne for chin retrusion reported improved chin projection and low rates of treatment-related events, per trade press.[19]

Registered trials for chin products include Restylane Lyft with lidocaine (NCT05777759, n=175), Restylane Defyne (NCT03624816, n=140), a new dermal filler for chin correction (NCT04631263, n=140), Stylage XXL in Chinese adults (NCT05009381, n=174), Restylane Shaype versus Juvederm Volux (NCT06336772, n=40), an Art Filler Volume study with a non-comparative chin arm (NCT04645576, n=98), a technique-and-product study (NCT07193199, n=21), and a phase 4 evaluation recruiting in 2026 (NCT07777926).[4][5][6][13][14][15][26][27]

timeline.event: Karl Meyer and John Palmer first isolate hyaluronic acid from cattle vitreous.[18]
Aufricht reports combined nose and chin surgery, an early chin augmentation reference.[10]
Dermal fillers come into wide use for wrinkles and volume loss.[17]
Restylane Defyne first approved in the US for deep facial wrinkles and folds.[19]
A case review of combined forehead, nose and chin filler is published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology.[1]
Juvederm Voluma XC receives FDA approval for chin augmentation (June), per trade press.[20]
Restylane Defyne is approved for mild to moderate chin retrusion (February).[19]
The Complications in Medical Aesthetics Collaborative publishes a guideline on managing hyaluronic acid filler vascular occlusion.[21]
A tongue-necrosis case series and a cadaveric anatomy study of the chin are published.[2][3]
Case report of vascular occlusion after low-volume chin filler managed with hyaluronidase.[7]

lore.intro: Members of looksmax.org discuss chin filler as a temporary, reversible way to test or improve chin projection, and some post self-injection results.[8][9][12]

claims.claim: Chin filler can approximate the look of surgery without surgery
claims.believers: Posters share before-and-after photographs and say filler added visible projection and helped them judge whether to pursue an implant or genioplasty.[9][12]
claims.experts: Manufacturer-registered trials have studied filler for chin retrusion and a case review reported profile changes, but surgical summaries say bone-based changes usually produce a more dramatic correction.[1][4][10]

claims.claim: The chin is a safe area to inject
claims.believers: Members of self-injection threads describe chin filler as a procedure they performed on themselves or friends and report it as a success.[16]
claims.experts: Authors of case series state the chin is considered safe but report rare vascular occlusion, necrosis and tongue necrosis; an anatomical study maps vessels to reduce embolization risk.[2][3][7]

claims.claim: Self-injected chin filler gives results comparable to a clinic
claims.believers: Some members post self-administered results with photographs and say they were satisfied.[16]
claims.experts: No published study has evaluated self-administered chin filler; the safety literature concerns anatomy and complications in clinical practice.[2][3]

claims.claim: Filler is a reversible way to preview a chin implant
claims.believers: Forum users describe filler as a trial run before committing to a permanent procedure.[8][9]
claims.experts: Hyaluronic acid filler can be degraded with hyaluronidase, and surgeons note that filler and implants differ in durability and in how precisely they shape the chin.[10][18][20][21]

claims.claim: Filler lasts as long as an implant if you top it up
claims.believers: Some members describe filler as a lower-cost alternative to implants or genioplasty.[8]
claims.experts: Hyaluronic acid chin filler is reported to last about 9 to 12 months, requiring touch-ups, whereas implant results are generally permanent.[20]

claims.claim: Combining jaw and chin filler transforms the lower face
claims.believers: Posters share jaw-plus-chin transformation photographs and discuss cheek hollows alongside chin work.[9][12]
claims.experts: A case review and a profile algorithm describe multi-site filler for profile change, and registered trials include a jaw-contouring filler study.[1][24]
